To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the convergent-discriminant validity data are not decisive in the sense that they are not sufficient to confirm or disconfirm a given hypothesis of validity, that they are not even necessary in the sense that a given hypothesis of construct validity is not disconfirmed by the failure to obtain the expected convergent-discriminate data, and that they can be misleading in the sense that the expected data are not obtained in many instances in which the hypothesis of validity is true.

(1) convergence is not necessary for validity, (2) discrimination is not necessary for the disconfirmation of a hypothesis of validity, and (3) the practical utility of a multitrait multimethod matrix is limited to the extent that its elements are not all known with certainty
(a) convergence does not necessarily indicate construct validity and (b) discrimination does not necessarily indicate discriminant validity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: (1) The conditions necessary to establish convergent or discriminant validity.
the following questions: (1) Under what conditions is it appropriate to infer that a set of measurements are valid?
the question of how to interpret the data of the multitrait multimethod analysis.

convergent and discriminat validity data are not in themselves conclusive evidence of validity, but that they may be so if certain prerequisites are satisfied, and that even if the prerequisites are not satisfied, they may be useful for other purposes.
convergent and discriminat validity data are generally too indecsive to support a strong conclusion about validity.
convergent and discriminative validity data are not in themselves sufficient for validity, but are necessary conditions for validity.

the data do not support or disconfirm the validity of the measures, but do support the hypothesis that the measures are not valid.

, when it comes to validity, convergence is not necessarily a good thing.
